$comment: ARINC 429 golden vectors. The ARINC 429 specification is a paid document, so every value here comes from public vendor application notes that were cross-checked against each other; each entry names its source and whether it was quoted or derived. Label-to-parameter assignments and equipment-ID tables are deliberately absent — they live in the paid spec and in per-aircraft ICDs. DO NOT MODIFY.

$labelBitOrderConflict.$note: Public sources agree the label is sent ahead of the rest of the word and in the opposite bit order to every other field, but they DISAGREE on which numbered bit holds the octal label's most significant bit. The two readings bit-reverse the label byte, so a decoder must not guess silently.

bit1-msb.meaning: Octal label MSB sits at word bit 1, LSB at bit 8; the label byte in the 32-bit value is the bit-reverse of the octal number.
bit1-msb.evidence: Holt Table 2 annotates ARINC bit 1 as 'Label (MSB)' and ARINC bit 8 as 'Label (LSB)' in both CR11 modes. Wikipedia/Holt: to transmit label 213 octal (8B hex) the bit-reversed value D1 hex is written to the label octet.

bit8-msb.meaning: Octal label MSB sits at word bit 8, LSB at bit 1; the label byte in the 32-bit value reads directly as the octal number.
bit8-msb.evidence: Transmission order is published as 8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1,9,10,...,32 with the note that the label's most significant bit is transmitted first, which places the MSB at bit 8. GE Table 6 tabulates a discrete word whose 'Label 005' has bit 1 = 1, bit 2 = 0, bit 3 = 1, bits 4-8 = 0 — that is 005 octal only when bit 8 is the MSB.

bcd.$note: Five subfields, MSD in bits 29-27 (3 bits, 0-7), then 26-23, 22-19, 18-15, 14-11 (4 bits, 0-9).

cases.$note: Last nibble is 0xA — not a decimal digit. The 3-bit MSD can never be invalid, which is why only subfields 2-5 are checked.

bnr.$source: ge Figure 7 and p.8, aim p.14
bnr.$note: Bit 29 is the sign (1 = negative / South / West / Left / From / Below); bit 28 carries half the parameter's full-scale value, bit 27 a quarter, and so on. Negative values are the two's complement of the positive value across bits 29-11.

cases.$quoted: scale 512, bits 29 through 19 used, bit 29 = 0 so the value is positive, bit 28 = 256, bit 23 = 1/64 of scale, bit 22 = 1/128 of scale, total 268
cases.$note: Field value derived from the quoted set bits 28, 23 and 22.
Two's complement of the case above across bits 29-11: 2^19 - 137216.
